THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.VISHWAJITH SHETTY
ORAL ORDER

(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.VISHWAJITH SHETTY) Accused Nos.5 and 6 are before this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in C.C.No.2754/2023, pending before the Court of Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Sindagi, arising out of Private Complaint No.20/2019, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 465,
468 and 474 of IPC.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the private complaint has been filed in the present case without complying the requirement of law as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Priyanka Srivastava vs. State of U.P. and another1.

entities.text: Priyanka Srivastava vs. State of U.P. and another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that there is total non-compliance of Sections 154(1) and 154(3) of Cr.P.C. in the present case.
Therefore, the learned Magistrate was not justified in referring the complaint to police under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. and therefore the entire proceedings gets vitiated.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
4. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for respondent No.1 and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 have opposed the petition.

Learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that there is a specific mention in the private complaint that the complainant had Shamshad Begum And Anr vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178394082/
2 visited Sindagi Police Station to lodge a complaint, but they have refused to receive the (2015) 6 SCC 287 NC: 2025:KHC-K:918 complaint.

entities.text: Shamshad Begum And Anr vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, there is compliance of Section 154(1) of Cr.P.C. in the present case.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Section 154 of Cr.P.C. reads as follows:
"154 - Information in cognizable cases -(1) Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, shall be reduced to writing by him or under his direction, and be read over to the informant; and every such information, whether given in writing or reduced to writing as aforesaid, shall be signed by the person giving it, and the substance thereof shall be entered in a book to be kept by such officer in such form as the State Government may prescribe in this behalf.
Provided that if the information is given by the woman against whom an offence under section 326A, section 326B, section 354, section 354A, section 354B, section 354C, section 354D, section 376, section 376A, section2 376AB, section 376B, section 376C, section 376D, section 376DA, section 376DB, section 376E or NC:
2025:KHC-K:918 section 509 of the Indian Penal Code is alleged to have been committed or attempted, then such information shall be recorded, by a woman police officer or any woman officer;1

Provided further that-- (a) in the event that the person against whom an offence under section 354, section 354A, section 354B, section 354C, section 354D, section 376, section 376A, section2 376AB, section 376B, section 376C, section 376D, section 376DA, section 376DB,
section 376E or section 509 of the Indian Penal Code is alleged to have been committed or attempted, is temporarily or permanently mentally or physically disabled, then such information shall be recorded by a police officer, at the residence of the person seeking to report such offence or at a convenient place of such person's choice, in the presence of an interpreter or a special educator, as the case may be;

(3) Any person, aggrieved by a refusal on the part of an officer in charge of a police station to record the information referred to in Sub-Section (1) may send the substance of such information, in writing and by post, to the Superintendent of Police concerned who, if satisfied that such information discloses the commission of a cognizable offence, shall either investigate the case himself or direct an investigation to be made by any police officer subordinate to him, in the manner provided by this Code, and such officer shall have all the powers of an officer in charge of the police Shamshad Begum And Anr vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178394082/
3 station in relation to that offence."

entities.text: Shamshad Begum And Anr vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. From a reading of the aforesaid provision of law, it is very clear that in the event any person is aggrieved by a refusal on the part of Police Officer in- charge of the police station to register FIR, he may send NC: 2025:KHC-K:918 the substance of such information in writing by post to the Superintendent of Police concerned and if the higher officer is satisfied that a case is made out for committing a cognizable offence, he shall either investigate the case or direct the Police Officer subordinate to him to investigate the case in accordance with law.
7.

In the case on hand, though a mention has been made in the private complaint that the complainant had visited Sindagi Police Station to lodge a complaint but the police had refused to receive the same
, there is no such mention in the complaint that he had complied the requirement of Section 154(3) of Cr.P.C.

Even to show compliance of Section 154(1) of Cr.P.C., except the self serving statement of the complainant as found in the private complaint, she has not produced any material along with the complaint to show that she had approached the police.

She has also not stated anything about compliance of Sections 154(1) or 154(3) of Cr.P.C. in her sworn statement nor any material was produced before NC: 2025:KHC-K:918 the learned Magistrate during the course of recording her sworn statement about compliance of Sections 154(1) and 154(3) of Cr.P.C.
8.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Priyanka Srivastava (supra), has observed that learned Magistrate before referring a private complaint to the Police under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. needs to satisfy himself about the fact that the complainant has complied the requirement of Sections 154(1)
and 154(3) of Cr.P.C. before filing the private complaint seeking reference under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C.

Since the same is not complied in the present case, entire proceedings gets vitiated and therefore, prosecution of the petitioners for the alleged offences based on such a private complaint would amount to abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, following order is passed:
ORDER
The criminal petition is allowed.

468 and 474 of IPC, as against the petitioners/accused Nos.5 and 6 stands quashed.
